# SK3005 — A task is discarded in synchronous code

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A task-producing invocation is used as a bare statement in a synchronous body.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Async |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

Discarding a task means the caller observes neither completion nor failure. An exception can surface later as an unobserved fault while the synchronous method has already reported success.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
void Start() { SaveAsync(); }
```

Write:

```csharp
Task StartAsync() => SaveAsync();
```

## When it does not fire

The rule reports only a bare invocation whose resolved return type derives from `Task`, inside a synchronous method, local function, lambda or constructor. Async bodies are left to compiler diagnostic CS4014. Assigning to a discard, storing, returning, awaiting or otherwise composing the task is treated as an explicit lifetime decision. No fix is offered because changing the containing API to async is a caller-wide refactor.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK3005.severity`
